note: Mutation radius. The argus may change which model a cell runs, numeric params (caps, tiers) and -- since text slots joined it -- the TEXT a cell reads (a tool description, a prompt block, a curator knob), each class listed in `rule:slot-classes`. Topology it may only PROPOSE. The radius widens by editing this row -- never by editing code. What it can REACH is narrower than what it may decide: a params update lands only on a cell type that has a params lane, so an `llm` cell's model and numeric knobs are in range and a `code` cell's cap (collector `max_iter`) is not -- see `params.numeric_param_keys` of `./mutator`; and a text change reaches only the cells a parent wired the `slot_update` lane to. Taking `text_slots` out of this row stops every text change at the mutator, the way back included.
A cycle without a pre-authored revert plan is invalid. The argus must know the way back BEFORE it moves, or the first surprise leaves the colony in a state nobody designed.
Hard cap per cycle. A control loop that can spend without a ceiling is an outage waiting for a slow night.
How far the quality metric may move against us before a change is reverted, in percent. Zero means: not at all. Quality is a gate, not a wish.
How long the post-change health check may take before the cycle treats the colony as unhealthy and reverts.

Prices per million tokens as `model=input/output,model=input/output`. Charter DATA rather than a provider call: a colony that has to reach the network to know what it spent cannot measure itself while the network is what broke. Empty on a fresh instance -- an unpriced model measures as zero cost, which is why the cost goal ships disabled.

The smallest validation batch a text change may be applied on. The loop takes the LARGER of this and the goal's own `min_samples`: a text change judged on ten conversations is a coin toss with a receipt, and a loop that applies coin tosses oscillates.

The classes of text the argus may change on its own, each only behind an evaluation batch. A class not listed here is refused with `key_outside_radius_<class>` -- the list widens by editing this row, never by editing code.
Text the argus may PROPOSE and never apply. How the colony speaks and how it behaves towards the people it serves is the owner's decision; a better number is an argument for it, not a licence.

Text the argus may not touch at all, not even as a proposal. Who the colony is does not move because a metric moved -- this check runs before every other one, so no radius edit and no argument from the judge reaches it.
